agree.reason: This owner pays her cousin $600 a year, and the page never tells her she can keep him for her taxes, so she sees $199 a month, which is $2,388 a year, as replacing someone she likes at four times the cost, and she probably won't book.

honest.reason: Every number matches the brief, and the $800 being about four months of fees is accurate, though the general line that accountants charge by the time spent sorting your numbers is stated as a fact without support.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the $800 as four months of fees, but it never puts the 3 misses as 9 of 12 months on time, never says that no client has left for any reason except selling their salon, and never sets the annual cost against what clean books save at tax time.

right_comparison.reason: The reader's real alternative is year-end books from a relative for $600, and the page describes it only as a generic accountant, without saying that her accountant or tax preparer keeps doing her tax return and simply gets clean books.

qualification.reason: The promise that the month is free if the books aren't closed by the 10th, starting in January, names a date and a consequence she can check, and the 30-day notice is just as concrete.

objections.reason: Her two objections, her cousin and the cost, go unanswered, and the price-rise section creates a worry without the reason the facts provide (payroll was added), while the six years of managing a salon and the limit of about five new clients are left out.

fit.reason: It is about 330 words of sales-page copy with clear sections and ends with a booking button, which matches what the brief asked for.
